answer: An attestation mesh with a time-separation bar: an attestation pays at close if countersigned by two identities whose last attestation is at least 12 epochs older than the signer's. Fresh clones lack aged witnesses, so each waits out a zero-payout window until the farm's oldest member passes the bar. Attacker cost: each clone is liveness-paid dead weight earning nothing, so scaling multiplies overhead, not payout. A ridge of aged signers bounds the horizon of a close; the opal is the age stamp on each countersignature, and a per-close trellis of countersigners stays auditable offline.
